podcast.title: Marriage to Win Butler (2003)
podcast.body: Regine Chassagne and Win Butler, after meeting in 2001 and forming an early version of Arcade Fire, were married in 2003. "They got married in 2003."

podcast.title: Birthplace and Family History
podcast.body: Regine Chassagne was born in Montreal to parents who had emigrated from Haiti in 1962, seeking refuge from the dictatorship of Papa Dr. Valier. Her family history includes the tragic Jeremy Vespers massacre of 1964, where some of her relatives were killed, emphasizing the context of her parents' move. "She was born in Montreal to parents from Haiti. They had moved to Quebec in 1962 to escape the craziness that was the dictatorship of Papa Dr. Valier."

podcast.title: McGill Jazz Voice Student
podcast.body: Regine Chassagne met Win Butler in Montreal in 2001 while she was studying jazz voice at McGill University, a pivotal encounter for the formation of Arcade Fire. "Regina and Wins met in 2001 while Regina was studying jazz voice at McGill."

podcast.title: Multi-Instrumentalist Skills
podcast.body: Win Butler was deeply impressed by Regine Chassagne's ability to play a wide array of instruments, including keyboards, organ, accordion, drums, and xylophone, which prompted him to invite her to join his band. "Wins was really impressed the way she could play just about any instrument, keyboards, organ, accordion, drum, cellophone."

xref.title: Montreal Religious Studies
xref.body: After prep school, Win Butler moved to Montreal to pursue religious studies, first at Concordia University and then at McGill University, which is where he would eventually meet his future bandmate and wife, Regine Chassagne. "Meanwhile, Wins moved to Montreal because he wanted to study religion, first to Concordia, then a McGill."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Who the Hell is Arcade Fire? Part 1

xref.title: Philanthropic Efforts in Haiti
xref.body: The band maintains a deep and growing relationship with Haiti, stemming from Regine Chassagne's family fleeing dictator Papa Doc Duvalier's forces for Montreal in the early 1960s. They have donated at least one million dollars to Haitian relief, working with the NGO Partners in Health. Following the devastating 2010 earthquake, band members made regular, unassuming trips to Haiti to provide on-the-ground assistance. "A big chunk of the money they've made, a million dollar chunk was donated to a Haitian relief organization."
